questions.q: What does the Script Debugger actually debug?
options: SQL queries sent directly to the underlying database
Server-side script execution — Business Rules, Script Includes, and background scripts running on the platform's JavaScript engine
Only CSS and layout issues on a form
Only Client Scripts running in the browser
questions.explain: The Script Debugger attaches to server-side script execution — the same engine covered in Chapter 2 — not browser-side code.

options: The Business Rule is skipped entirely and never runs
The Incident record is automatically deleted
The transaction pauses the instant execution reaches that line, letting you inspect variables before continuing
ServiceNow throws a syntax error and the update fails
questions.explain: A breakpoint pauses execution at that exact line — it doesn't skip, delete, or error; it just freezes the transaction for inspection.

questions.q: What's the difference between "step over" and "step into" while paused at a breakpoint?
options: Step over runs the current line and moves to the next one without following any function it calls; step into follows execution inside that called function
They are two names for the exact same action
Step into exits the debugger entirely; step over does nothing
Step over deletes the current line; step into adds a new line
questions.explain: Step over stays at the current level of execution; step into descends into whatever function the current line calls.

questions.q: Which scenario is the Script Debugger NOT able to help with?
options: Stepping line by line through a method while your session is attached
A Business Rule configured to run asynchronously, queued to execute outside your attached session
A Script Include method called directly from a background script you run and watch
A synchronous before-update Business Rule you trigger yourself by saving a record
questions.explain: The debugger only works for synchronous execution attached to your own session — async, queued execution runs outside that session entirely.

questions.q: Why can't the Script Debugger ever be used to debug a Client Script?
options: The Script Debugger only supports Business Rules, never Script Includes
Client Scripts are written in a completely different programming language
Client Scripts don't contain any real JavaScript code
Client Scripts run as real JavaScript in the user's browser, not on the server where the Script Debugger attaches
questions.explain: The Script Debugger is a server-side tool. Client Scripts execute client-side, in the browser — a different runtime entirely, covered in Lesson 28.
